newsArray.title: IND vs NZ 2nd T20I: Shreyas Iyer Just 25 Runs Away From Breaking Rohit Sharma’s Big Record
newsArray.description: Shreyas Iyer has a significant opportunity to put his name alongside some of cricket’s leading T20 records when India take on New Zealand in the second match of their five-game series today, October 24, at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. The India skipper has enjoyed a productive year in the shortest international format and is now within touching distance of a mark set by former captain Rohit Sharma. A strong performance against New Zealand could also bring him closer to a T20 record associated with Pakistan’s Babar Azam. Iyer Needs 25 Runs To Move Past Rohit Shreyas Iyer has accumulated 632 runs in 22 T20Is as India captain in 2026. That leaves him just 25 runs short of Rohit Sharma’s tally of 656, scored across 29 matches as captain in 2022. Having taken over the leadership role from Suryakumar Yadav in June, Iyer has had a relatively better impact with the bat. Reaching the milestone would see him establish a new run-scoring benchmark for India’s T20I captains in a calendar year. Rohit’s record came during a year in which he led India through a demanding international schedule. The former skipper also guided the team to the T20 World Cup title in 2024, adding to his legacy in the format. Babar Azam’s Global Record Remains The Bigger Target Beyond the Indian record, Iyer has another milestone within reach across T20 cricket. He has scored 1,130 runs as captain in T20 matches this year and needs 96 more to overtake Babar Azam’s 1,225-run tally from 35 matches in 2021. Babar continues to hold the record for the most runs scored by a captain in T20 internationals in a calendar year, having made 939 runs in 29 matches as Pakistan skipper in 2021. Iyer’s immediate focus may be on winning the match and extending the series lead, but another substantial innings could bring the global T20 milestone into sharper focus as well.
creator: suyash sahay

newsArray.title: KCC clinches Khalsa Premier League 2026 title
newsArray.description: Sunderbani, Oct 23: The grand finale of the Khalsa Premier League (KPL) First Edition 2026 was played between Khalsa Cricket Club and Singh Warriors Cricket Club at M.A. Stadium, Jammu. In an exciting final, Khalsa Cricket Club, as per a statement issued, emerged victorious by successfully chasing the target of 183 runs in 18.4 overs and lifted the prestigious KPL First Edition 2026 trophy. After winning the toss, Khalsa Cricket Club elected to field first. Batting first, Singh Warriors Cricket Club put up a competitive total of 182 runs for the loss of 6 wickets in 20 overs. In reply, Khalsa Cricket Club displayed an impressive batting performance, achieving the target in just 18.4 overs and securing the championship title. Arun Gupta, President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Jammu, graced the occasion as the Chief Guest, while S. Baljeet Singh (JKPS), SP North Jammu, attended as the Guest of Honour. The Chief Guest congratulated the winning team on its outstanding performance and appreciated the organising committee for successfully conducting the tournament. He also lauded the efforts of the organisers in providing a positive platform for young players to showcase their cricketing talent and promoting sportsmanship among the youth. The tournament was organised by S. Avtar Singh Khalsa, S. Balvinder Singh Soodan, S. Chamkor Singh, S. Hardeep Singh, and S. Ravpreet Singh, who ensured that the league was conducted in a disciplined, systematic, and sporting manner. The organisers highlighted that the primary objective of the Khalsa Premier League was not merely to promote cricket but also to deliver a strong social message against drug abuse and gangster culture. Through sports, the organisers aimed to encourage young people to adopt a healthy lifestyle, develop discipline, and channel their energy towards constructive activities. While addressing the media and the gathering, S. Balvinder Singh expressed his heartfelt gratitude to all the spectators, media representatives, M.A. Stadium staff, distinguished guests, and everyone who supported and encouraged the players throughout the tournament. He particularly thanked the guests who took time out of their busy schedules to attend the matches and motivate the participating teams. He also appreciated the cooperation and coordination of all those who contributed to the successful organisation of the league. Singh emphasised that the enthusiastic participation of the public and the consistent support of the guests had strengthened the organisers' resolve to continue promoting sports as an effective means of engaging youth in positive activities. The successful conclusion of the Khalsa Premier League First Edition 2026 marked an important step towards promoting cricket, strengthening community participation, and spreading the message of a drug-free society and a youth culture free from gangsterism. The organisers expressed their hope that the league would continue to grow in the coming years, providing more opportunities for young cricketers to showcase their talent while inspiring the next generation to embrace sports, discipline, unity, and social responsibility.
creator: gk news service
